HEADACHE RED FLAGS 
 
* Onset: Sudden/thunderclap, exertional, post traumatic 
* Symptoms: Altered mental state, seizure, focal neurology, meningism, visual changes, fever 
* Medications: ARVs, TB Rx, recent antimicrobials, immunosuppressants, anticoagulants/anti-platelet agents,  
   illicit drugs 
* History: No prior headaches, worst headache ever, worsening over weeks/months, immune compromise,  
   subtle neurology/cognitive decline 
*Comorbidities: Malignancy, immunosuppression, vasculitis, recent/current pregnancy, bleeding/clotting  
  disorders, poorly controlled HT, previous neurosurgery 
*Examination: Abnormal  vital signs, altered mental status, focal neurology, meningism, features  of raised ICP 
DISPOSITION 
 
§
Neuro/neurosurgical consult as appropriate 
§
Close monitoring for deterioration if secondary headache 
§
Consider outpatient Neurology review for primary headache 
syndromes 
SECONDARY HEADACHE  
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS 
 
•
Intracranial haemorrhage: Hx of trauma, hypertension, 
thunderclap headache, anticoagulant use 
•
Infection – intra OR extracranial: fever, vomiting, meningism, 
rash, photophobia.  NB Malaria! 
•
Space occupying lesions: High index of suspicion in HIV, 
progressive symptoms, focal neurology 
•
Carotid/vertebrobasilar dissection: Neck pain, cerebellar or 
cranial nerve fallout, trivial trauma 
•
Cerebral venous thrombosis: Gradual onset, facial 
swelling/erythema, subtle CT findings often missed! 
•
Temporal arteritis: Jaw pain, tender temporal area/scalp, 
absent temporal artery pulsation 
•
Acute hydrocephalus: Structural abnormalities, post infective, 
previous shunt 
•
Hypertensive encephalopathy: Poorly controlled, 
hypertensive emergency 
•
Pre-eclampsia: ALWAYS check pregnancy test! 
•
Acute angle closure glaucoma: Visual loss, painful red eye, 
pupillary defect, raised IOP 
•
Carbon monoxide toxicity: Fire in enclosed space 
•
ENT/dental pathology: Infective, traumatic, chronic 
•
Shunt failure/pathology: Prior neurosurgery/hydrocephalus
